new_findings.authority_qualification: The return still correctly keeps execution_authorized, implementation_proven and m4_accepted false. That does not make contradictory semantic-contract and assertion credit sound.
new_findings.impact: An unexpected write on a no-write/replay branch can be treated as another verified durable effect rather than a branch violation. This is an internal identity/disposition contradiction already expressible in the implemented offline contract, not a missing runtime observation adapter.
new_findings.problem: The new tested-effect reconciliation is one-directional. It requires a matching original mutation for a replay and skips that requirement for no_write, but never rejects a ledger mutation attributed to the current tested invocation when the complete response says no_write or replay. A replay can also use the tested invocation as its own supposed original mutation.
new_findings.recommendation: Consider enforcing the inverse disposition invariant: a no_write or replay disposition cannot have a new-effect ledger row for the current tested invocation. For replay, require the original mutation invocation to differ from the replay invocation and retain the existing required original kind/oracle join. Preserve unrelated prior effects. Add early/late negative controls that append a current-invocation mutation without removing any original obligation, and replay self-original controls. If the ledger is intended to describe underlying effects rather than actual mutating invocations, make that distinct identity explicit instead of reusing invocation_sha256.
reproduction: Start from the independently constructed valid v2 no_write packet: R1.tested_effect={kind:no_write,mutation_invocation_sha256:null,oracle_sha256:null}; R2 carries a complete no_write response; R3 contains a verified unrelated prior probe; the baseline passes.

Keep that prior probe unchanged. Add a second R3 row with invocation_sha256 equal to R1.tested_invocation_sha256/R2.invocation_sha256, effect=publication, the expected mutation oracle, recovery=verified and a registered evidence reference.
Bind R1.effect_ledger_sha256 to the resulting immutable definitions and reseal the entire included controller chain. Every individual v2 envelope and typed reference remains valid.
reconcile returns structural_and_semantic_contract_valid=true while R9.atomicity and R9.durability remain pass, despite the same invocation being both no-write and an acknowledged new publication.

The acceptance occurs for early and late complete responses. Publication/backpressure replay packets likewise pass if a current-invocation mutation is added alongside the correctly joined original mutation. Replay self-original identity variants also pass.
new_findings.title: No-write/replay responses can coexist with a new mutation by the same tested invocation

original_findings.closure_basis: A valid v2 packet passes first. Altering only included R4 bytes, with all independently supplied contexts unchanged and all individual envelopes still valid, rejects with INCLUDED_CHAIN. Continuous sequence-zero chains, actual predecessor hashes and stable per-role issuer identities are enforced; dictionary iteration order is not confused with sequence order.

The original mutating tested-ACK omission, now expressed in the accepted v2 schema, rejects with TESTED_ACK_EFFECT_MISSING. Early and late publication/backpressure/replay joins also reject missing or mismatched mutation identity, effect kind and oracle. Legitimate no-write and replay counterparts pass.
original_findings.qualification: This closes the original borrowed-probe counterexample, not every new disposition invariant. The inverse contradiction introduced by the new no-write/replay fields is tracked separately as COR-C0-006.

original_findings.closure_basis: Decoded, exact-layout witnesses still validate structurally but wrong heartbeat/P3 ordinals reject as ORDINAL/FRAME_STATE. Supported held cases now check exact transcript/value and prototype/PC state, plus zero heartbeat outside the helper case. Positive native-state models remain accepted; heartbeat motion and client receive evidence remain external.

The original decoded wrong VM completion rejects with FINAL_EFFECTS; N final credit rejects with FINAL_CASE; wrong P1 final ordinal rejects with FINAL_TRANSCRIPT. All 240 positive case IDs accept their independently modeled correct final state and all 36 F/N IDs reject successful final credit.

Missing stop proof in a schema-valid, consistently resealed packet rejects fault-scoped passes as FAULT_NOT_PROVED and verified ledger recovery as RECOVERY_WITHOUT_FAULT. Failure/unproven packets remain representable rather than being relabeled successes.

report_preservation: Created exclusively with one final LF and made read-only. Later reviews must use a distinct report; the original correctness/review.json remains unchanged.
strengths: All eight original invalid acceptance examples now reject for their intended semantic reasons, not merely new-schema field mismatch.
The oracle now has exact typed held/final predicates across the fixed native families, with N/F final-success exclusions.
The included-chain reconstruction is independent of caller-provided predecessor expectations and closes the original stale-journal splice.
The reference kinds/process joins and explicit deny-all no-regrant check preserve important distinctions between state, BOOT and credential retirement.
The README continues to accurately separate offline artifact preparation from executable assembly and runtime evidence.
summary: The original five findings are closed for their demonstrated acceptance counterexamples using accepted v2 schema fixtures and specific semantic rejection reasons. The remediation materially improves chain, tested-effect, witness and stop-proof checks. One new P1 blocker remains: complete no-write/replay dispositions can contradict same-invocation mutation rows while retaining semantic/atomicity/durability credit. This verdict is on the implementation-only artifact foundation, not executable OBS1.
